LESSON: GRAMMAR IN USE 14.3.1 SENTENCES- DIRECT AND INDIRECT SPEECH

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade 9
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 14
Topic 14.3: Grammar in use 14.3.1 Sentences- Direct and Indirect Speech
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Grammar in use 14.3.1 Sentences- Direct and Indirect Speech, part of Strand 14 in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade 9 ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: How do we report what others have said?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. recognize signs of words related to the theme,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Grammar in use 14.3.1 Sentences- Direct and Indirect Speech in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. differentiate between direct and indirect speech,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Grammar in use 14.3.1 Sentences- Direct and Indirect Speech in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. convert direct speech into indirect speech,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Grammar in use 14.3.1 Sentences- Direct and Indirect Speech in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. use the correct punctuation marks in direct speech,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Grammar in use 14.3.1 Sentences- Direct and Indirect Speech in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

E. apply direct and indirect speech correctly in communication • In groups or pairs, learner is guided to observe a signed video with words related to the theme, fingerspell and sign. • Individually, learner is guided to sign read provided sentences or paragraphs to learn how direct and indirect speech appear in writing. • Individually, learner is guided to convert sentences written in direct speech into indirect speech and vice versa. • Individually, learner is guided to insert the correct punctuation marks in sentences to mark direct speech. • In pairs, learners are guided to rewrite reported questions. • In pairs, learners are guided to compose sentences in direct and indirect speech How do we report what others have said? 179

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Grammar in use 14.3.1 Sentences- Direct and Indirect Speech together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication and collaboration: teamwork skills as learners work together to complete exercises.

• Self-efficacy- effective communication skills as learners gain confidence to write direct and indirect speech correctly in

communication.

Values:
● Responsibility: learners work in pairs to compose sentences in direct and indirect speech.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
● Learner Support Programme-Problem solving: is enhanced as learners work together to covert sentences from direct to

indirect speech and vice versa.

SECTION 6: SUMMARY

Main points to remember:

1. recognize signs of words related to the theme,
2. differentiate between direct and indirect speech,
3. convert direct speech into indirect speech,
4. use the correct punctuation marks in direct speech,
